description:
Update - I changed this to Hycrocybe based on the texture of the cap surface and it's convex shape. However, it doesn't look like there are any recorded pink Hycrocybes in North America.

The spore print is white.

This article on North American hycrocybes is interesting.
http://www.fs.fed.us/nrs/pubs/jrnl/2014/nrs_2014_lodge_001.pdf



_______________________

So far this keys out as Mycena adonis ( which is actually a large group of species ). But I am thinking now it is not Mycena as the cap shape is wrong and the cap surface texture is wrong.

The gills and stem look correct for Mycena.

This single small mushroom was growing from the ground out of general mixed hardwood and pine woods. There was white mycelium nearby but it was not connected to it. When I dug it up, it was rooted and I saw no mycelium.

The cap is just at 1 cm across. The stem is 4-6 times longer than the cap size. 

This mushroom is pink. The stem is translucent pink. The gills are pink and the cap is pink.

I crushed the base of the stem and it smelled like chlorophyll, like chewing on grass blades.

I am trying to get a spore print.

The gills are wide spaced with a shorter intermediate gill at the outer edge, see photos.

description:
Hongos entomopatógeno, el insecto es una cigarra estado de pupa. Se encontró enterrada.


Datos de Yopal: registrado en Bosque Seco Tropical (temporada de lluvia). Precipitación mínima de 15 – 25 mm en los meses de enero y diciembre, precipitación máxima 350 mm y 300 mm en los meses de mayo, junio y julio; con menos de 60 mm de lluvia en el mes más seco y precipitación anual superior a 1270 mm. Cuenta con valores mínimos de humedad relativa a inicio del año (65%), y valores más altos en junio, julio, agosto y septiembre (90-85%). Cuenta con una altura sobre el nivel del mar entre 0 y 1000 m, una pluviosidad entre 2000 y 4000 mm y temperatura promedio mayor de 24 °C, con amplitud de temperatura máxima de 8 °C, como se referencia en DANE. Los máximos valores de temperatura no sobrepasan los 36 °C y los mínimos valores no logran bajar los 19 °C que se presentan en febrero y en julio, respectivamente. Temperatura media anual mayor de 20 °C, con una estación seca y una lluviosa bien definidas (Bustamante et al., 2017; DANE, 1999; Castro y Sosa, 2017).

Se observa con frecuencia plantas representativas de la zona como Yarumo (Cecropia peltata), Jobo (Spondias mombin), Cedro (Cedrela odorata), Nauno (Albizzia guachepele), Cañafistol (Cassia moschata), Flor blanco (Tabebuia orinocensis), Uña de gato (Cynodon dactylon), entre otras.

Te dejo algunas recomendaciones para tus registros. Las fotografías y descripciones que hagas, te van a permitir identificar el ejemplar: más detalles ver: https://colombia.inaturalist.org/journal/teodoro_chivatabedoya/54937-registro-de-hongos-macromicetos

-Tomar fotografías de las diferentes estructuras del basidioma/ascoma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), su estipe (píe), píleo (sombrero) y base. En el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada. Para trabajos de identificación, es necesario que retires el ejemplar completo, sin cortar o maltratar la base del estípite, de igual forma, tomar nota del tipo de sustrato (material donde crece y desarrolla).

-Es importante que describas las dimensiones (altura y diámetro), forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona y temporada en la que crecen, para hacer un seguimiento y logres observar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero).

-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura, tipo de bosque, insectos asociados, etc).

-No olvides que la determinación de macromicetos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de género y especie; en la mayoría) implica actividades de descripción morfológica externa e interna, esporada, reacciones químicas, microscopia e incluso herramientas moleculares (ADN/PCR).

Recomendaciones para su registro, descripción y posterior determinación:
-Fotografiar estructuras del basidioma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), en el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada.
-Es importante que describas las dimensiones, forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona (sustrato) para hacer un seguimiento y logres detallar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero)
-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura y tipo de bosque).
-No olvides que la determinación de hongos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de genero y especie; en la mayoría) implica otras actividades como descripción morfológica externa e interna, reacciones químicas, microscopia y ADN.

-Fotografiar estructuras del basidioma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), en el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada.
-Es importante que describas las dimensiones, forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona (sustrato) para hacer un seguimiento y logres detallar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero)
-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura y tipo de bosque).
-No olvides que la determinación de hongos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de genero y especie; en la mayoría) implica otras actividades como descripción morfológica externa e interna, reacciones químicas, microscopia y ADN.

description:
Species Name: Oak-loving Elfin Saddle

Kingdom: Fungi

Shape: Saddle-shaped caps of Helvella lacunosa often have three or more contorted lobes. The cap edges join to the stem to form a multi-lobed inner chamber with several openings.

Size: Typically 2 to 4cm across the cap, Elfin Saddle fungi have a total height 4 to 10cm.

Coloration: The smooth outer surface of the cap is dark grey and is the surface that bears the spores, while the infertile inner surface is also grey but has a felty feel. Longitudinally grooved and hollow, the stems are grey or grey-brown and often contain many inner chambers.

Characteristic: They have microscopic flask-shaped structures on the fertile cap surface that produce spores.

Reference: 

https://www.first-nature.com/fungi/helvella-lacunosa.php

Location: USF Riverfront Park, Tampa, FL, US

Habitat: This species seems to favor rich soil and burnt ground, against which as a background it is not at all conspicuous and so is easily missed. 

Distribution: A fairly common find in Britain and Ireland, Elfin Saddle fungus occurs also throughout mainland Europe, from Scandinavia right down to the southern shores of the Iberian Peninsula. This species is also found in North America

description:
Recomendaciones para su registro, descripción y posterior determinación:
-Fotografiar estructuras del basidioma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), en el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada.
-Es importante que describas las dimensiones, forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona (sustrato) para hacer un seguimiento y logres detallar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero)
-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura, tipo de bosque, etc).
-No olvides que la determinación de hongos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de genero y especie; en la mayoría) implica otras actividades como descripción morfológica externa e interna, reacciones químicas, microscopia y ADN.

description:
"{_DUE FUNGHI_}"({_two mushrooms_})In zona "collinare"(hills), trovati in un grande "castagneto"(chestnut forest ), 1000m dal livello del mare.soleggiato.
"Uno piccolo con cappello più curvo e quello grande con Cappello più piatto,senza anello."
(The small mushroom with curvy hat, the big mushroom with flat hat. Without ring)

These mushrooms were found in the grass area near my home back in Orlando. There were a total of six mushrooms all of which were circular, white, with a smooth surface, and a brown circle in the center. Upon further investigation I was able to conclude that the mushrooms were Marasmius oreades, or "fairy-ring mushrooms". These type of mushrooms are common in backyards, and are known to make a ring in a large grassy area due to fungi in the grass. "Fairy ring fungi do not attack grass directly but break down organic matter in the soil." 

Source: "Lawn Mushrooms and Fairy Rings", http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/help-for-the-home-gardener/advice-tips-resources/pests-and-problems/diseases/fairy-rings/lawn-mushrooms.aspx.

Recomendaciones para su registro, descripción y posterior determinación:
-Fotografiar estructuras del basidioma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), en el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada.
-Es importante que describas las dimensiones, forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona (sustrato) para hacer un seguimiento y logres detallar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero)
-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura, tipo de bosque, etc).
-No olvides que la determinación de hongos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de genero y especie; en la mayoría) implica otras actividades como descripción morfológica externa e interna, reacciones químicas, microscopia y ADN.

description:
These mushrooms were found in San Ramon, California in a grassy area off a trail on May 3rd, 2020. The identification of these mushrooms is Tricholoma Murrillianum.  

The observed behavior of these mushrooms was that they grew all next to each other not very spread out and were in a shaded area beneath a tree with grass and other a few other plants surrounding. Tricholoma Murrillianum has a few unique markings on top and has white-ish rounded tops. I found it while walking on the trail and was excited to find some bigger mushrooms. I like how rounded the tops are and they remind me of what I picture in my head when someone says mushrooms. 
After doing some research, I found that they are in fact edible and humans can eat Tricholoma Murrillianum. They are firm with good flavor, have a spicy odor, and have a meaty texture. 
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricholoma_murrillianum

Datos de Yopal: registrado en Bosque Seco Tropical (temporada de lluvia). Precipitación mínima de 15 – 25 mm en los meses de enero y diciembre, precipitación máxima 350 mm y 300 mm en los meses de mayo, junio y julio; con menos de 60 mm de lluvia en el mes más seco y precipitación anual superior a 1270 mm. Cuenta con valores mínimos de humedad relativa a inicio del año (65%), y valores más altos en junio, julio, agosto y septiembre (90-85%). Cuenta con una altura sobre el nivel del mar entre 0 y 1000 m, una pluviosidad entre 2000 y 4000 mm y temperatura promedio mayor de 24 °C, con amplitud de temperatura máxima de 8 °C, como se referencia en DANE. Los máximos valores de temperatura no sobrepasan los 36 °C y los mínimos valores no logran bajar los 19 °C que se presentan en febrero y en julio, respectivamente. Temperatura media anual mayor de 20 °C, con una estación seca y una lluviosa bien definidas (Bustamante et al., 2017; DANE, 1999; Castro y Sosa, 2017).

Se observa con frecuencia plantas representativas de la zona como Yarumo (Cecropia peltata), Jobo (Spondias mombin), Cedro (Cedrela odorata), Nauno (Albizzia guachepele), Cañafistol (Cassia moschata), Flor blanco (Tabebuia orinocensis), Uña de gato (Cynodon dactylon), entre otras.

Te dejo algunas recomendaciones para tus registros. Las fotografías y descripciones que hagas, te van a permitir identificar el ejemplar: más detalles ver: https://colombia.inaturalist.org/journal/teodoro_chivatabedoya/54937-registro-de-hongos-macromicetos

-Tomar fotografías de las diferentes estructuras del basidioma/ascoma/cuerpo fructifero/carpoforo/seta (por encima, por debajo y de perfil), su estipe (píe), píleo (sombrero) y base. En el caso de retirar el ejemplar sin conocerlo, debes comprometerte a realizar una descripción detallada para aportar a su conocimiento y que no quede en una muestra arrancada, fotografiada y desechada. Para trabajos de identificación, es necesario que retires el ejemplar completo, sin cortar o maltratar la base del estípite, de igual forma, tomar nota del tipo de sustrato (material donde crece y desarrolla).

-Es importante que describas las dimensiones (altura y diámetro), forma, consistencia, textura, color y olor. Recuerda que los ejemplares cambian bastante según su estado de desarrollo, así que es ideal familiarizarse con la zona y temporada en la que crecen, para hacer un seguimiento y logres observar la variabilidad fenotípica del basidioma o ascoma (cuerpo fructífero).

-Toma fotos del entorno y agrega datos del ecosistema (humedad, temperatura, altura, tipo de bosque, insectos asociados, etc).

-No olvides que la determinación de macromicetos es compleja y no se realiza únicamente con fotografías, esta tarea (a nivel de género y especie; en la mayoría) implica actividades de descripción morfológica externa e interna, esporada, reacciones químicas, microscopia e incluso herramientas moleculares (ADN/PCR).

description:
I was taking my dogs to the vet and thought initially this was some scat, after further "digging" into it I understood that it was a mushroom. Found growing outside of the clinic under two cultivated hardwood trees. My impression was that it could be a Lactarius species, but I was left speechless after what happened next. 

The first specimen I tried to pull out ended up in failure as I snapped the base off which left a majority of the fruit body in the ground. I thought this was odd, so for the next specimen I carefully dug around the base to find a massive sclerotia of mycelium! The sclerotia was about the same size as the stipe, which was unique to me as well (somewhat bulbous, short and stubbed). A couple of the photos (I think #2-3) were taken 30 seconds after holding the sclerotia under water, attempting to wash away the dirt and debris. 

The cross section of the specimen shows that it has an empty "pith" in the stipe, or is somewhat hollow as you can see. The sclerotia is just a hardened ball of dirt and mycelium, literally feels like a rock now. 

Usually I can put a genus to most of the fungi I see, but this one is different. Eventually I will update with additional information and photos of spores. I wish I would have taken better photos but my dogs were getting antsy.

Mag. 400x
Large, tetrahedral, asexual ascospore of an aquatic hyphomycetes fungi (known collectively as Ingoldian fungi).  Compare the current specimen with a smaller example from a previous observation, https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/105817766.  These are often involved in leaf litter decomposition.  Using Oliver Kim's (MicrobeHunter) video about "focus stacking" and the free software described, Picolay, I performed my first stacking experiment https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4reipg9LV8M.  Image 1 is a stacked image.  Image 2 is a composite of the 6 photos that were focus-stacked, using Picolay, to create the first image.  Considering that the focal planes represented by the 6 contributing photographs are too widely spaced (i.e, truly need more intervening images), the result is impressive.  I hope to play with Picolay again soon!.

description: Crust of warty aspect with fimbriate margin. Hardwoods. Mountain. Spores seem finely ornamented: 1.9 x 6.1 um. Basidia 31.2 x 5.4 um. Subicular hyphae looks finely ornamented/granulose 9.8 um. Margin has flat fan like  cordons growing under layer of hyphae. There are also other thick hyphae with drops and odd tips 2.9-4.9 um. Some hyphae have odd tips on the sides. It has an interesting smell like edamame. Not sure if the yellow cordons have any relation with it.

Hidden in leaf duff. On a petiole. Park. Interesting asexual stage. Two types of 'structures were seen. Some look like a lemon and the others look like bottles with crystals at top. The last ones get loose. They grow  on rows on septate hyphae. The fruitbody looks like a plume. Simple spores around 1.9 x 4.9 um. The other type are around 4.4um in high. Seems to belong to Moliniales but the family is not in inaturalist. Margarinomyces seems close to it.
Growing on a quasi dead nut tree. Park. Micro features information on photos.

description:
Possibly. Interior gelatinous, very sticky. Spores light brown, smooth walled. Growing in leaf litter, cypress, white oak, holly, beech, sourwood, tupelo, magnolia.  White rhizomorphs, fuzzy ball shaped exterior. 

Notes and last 6 photos by Django Grootmeyers:
Collected with, and found by, Alisha Millican. Growing scattered in leaf litter near Taxodium distichum, Quercus alba, Fagus grandifolia, Oxydendron arboreum, Nyssa sylvatica, Magnolia sp. and Ilex opaca. Basidiocarps reddish yellow (7.5YR 7/6 in Munsell); with fuzzy peridium; fragile and collapsing easily; attached by short stems to white to pale orange rhizomorphs; up to 18.1 mm wide. Gleba gelatinous. Lacking a clearly delimited columella. Odor not distinctive. Monomitic with simple-septate generative hyphae. Subhymenial hyphae gelatinized. Cystidia absent. Basidia 4-sterigmate. Spores smooth, pale brown, and thick-walled. Spore measurements: (5.9) 6.3 - 8.1 (8.6) × (2.6) 2.9 - 3.6 (3.8) µm; Q = (2) 2.1 - 2.4 (2.7); N = 30; Me = 7.3 × 3.2 µm; Qe = 2.3

NUMBER: 20220911
SPECIES: Peach-Colored Fly Agaric, Amanita persicina (Jenkins, 1977)
OTHER NAMES: Formerly considered a subspecies or variety of the famous Fly Agaric, A. muscaria (Linnaeus, 1753).  All these names remain in use and controversial.  Possibly a morphological species, which had been allowed in mycology for hundreds of years.
DISTINCTIONS: Upper cap 4-20 cm (1.6-7.8 in) wide, color dull reddish-orange adorned with numerous yellowish cottony warts, lower white; stem 8-25 cm (3.1-9.8 in) long, 1-3 cm (0.4-1.2 in) thick, usually tapering to apex and flaring to an enlarged basal bulb, white, ring composed of a few fragments or often none.
DATE, TIME: 11 September 2022, 12:07 PM
LOCALITY: Urban Estates, Vineyards, Florida
LATITUDE, LONGITUDE: 26.20674, 81.73381
DISTRIBUTION: Eastern USA, mostly Southeastern, Texas to Georgia, with records in New Jersey and New York.  Pinterest (2022) noted Amanita persicina in north Florida, but not in central or south Florida.  iNaturalist (unpublished) did not list this mushroom in south Florida.  Our record represents a range extension into south Florida.
USE and DANGER: Has a pleasant taste and odor and is both psychoactive and poisonous (if not properly prepared by parboiling).  This statement above should not be considered a recommendation concerning edibility or safety.  This is a dangerous mushroom for consumption (Mcarthy et al., 2022).
ECOLOGY: Mycorrhizal (symbiotic with tiny roots) with trees.  This one was near the base of a Southern Live Oak Tree, Quercus virginiana Miller, 1768.

description:
on Ulmus americana (or possibly alata). They grow at the base of the buds and only on one side of the twig, the lower "brown" side (the upper side is more gray). Typically one "body" per bud. I've been seeing these for 18 years, just like this. 

When wet, they plump up (see last photos for dry shots). 

Here's the first observation I made in 2005: https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/106470935

Here's my entry at bugguide: https://bugguide.net/node/view/2088360

I'm not sure the white watery blobs (photos 4 and 7) are related. I found a few of them on the tree itself when rain had just stopped. I closely examined many twigs on the tree two days in a row, one rainy and the next sunny. I've found some of the "bodies" on one of the trees itself but so far they are smaller than the ones I've been finding on the ground underneath the tree. 

I've been through the scales here and don't think I've found any matches: http://scalenet.info/associates/Ulmus%20americana/

Here's a definite scale from the same tree: https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/151059428

This is one of the elms I'm finding them under: https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/151217612

I did an experiment with a "plumped" one I found on wet ground after a rain. I brought it home and several hours later it was dried out and "deflated". I put it in a small bowl of water and checked it in 15 minutes to find that it had rehydrated again. See last 3 photos. 

I added a set for smaller ones found on a tree (not on the ground): https://www.inaturalist.org/observations/151839406

Mar 23: After a rain, I noticed quite a few of them forming ascocarp trype structure. 5 photos added.

description:
At least 5 fungus bodies were seen on 30 June 2023, occurring along a 3 metre section on the north edge of Dune Track at Langwarrin Flora and Fauna Reserve, Victoria. Fungal bodies were between 15 and 20mm high. The soil was pale sand with very short moss. Associated plants include Allocasuarina sp., Leptospermum myrsinoides, Epacris impressa, Drosera peltata, Lepidosperma sieberi, and occasional stunted Eucalyptus viminalis.

The bodies closely resemble photo 300b, Aphelaria sp., in the book "A Field Guide to Australian Fungi" by Bruce Fuhrer, published in 2005 by Bloomings Books, Melbourne. The habitat given in that book is "... In wet eucalypt and pine forest ..." whereas they were seen in heathland.

The first microscopy photo is in Melzer's reagent and the second in KOH. 

Currently spores seem to grow and germinate in culture.

That being said, I will not upload this to genbank until I know for certain that the sequence read is good. 

On another note hopefully I can find this again or can get multiple collections of this. I'll have to check the spot from last year.

description: Another one of those confections that makes my heart beat faster, and results in involuntary humming, trilling and whatnot. So much so this collection jumped the queue of specimens awaiting research and microscopy…Alas it looks like these are immature fruitbodies of a species that provokes a somewhat lower heart rate. Habitat: On mossy mudbank (see photo 5), in this collection, the fruitbodies were attached to mud at least not apparently/directly attached to moss filaments. Macro Summary: Fruitbody 2-4mm (see photo 6), sessile, spathulate, flabelliform, some like mini ladles/scoops (see photo 4), margin wavy/undulate in largest specimens and when dry, white/cream, flesh thin translucent when fresh, more stereoid-looking when dry. Upper sterile surface finely felty under lens (also see photo 2 and 7). Hymenophore nearly smooth, barely any folds/wrinkles, translucent (see photos 1 and 3). Micro Summary: Microscopy was a bit of a bust. I wasn’t able to find spores either in sections or via spore print. These may be immature fruitbodies. Nevertheless, adding photos of the narrow clavate basidia, what appear to be narrow cylindric cystidia and the piliepellis hyphae. Adding references below for future reference/microscopy attempts • Reference Material: o Correspondence with Prof Dennis Desjardin, 1-8-25 o Fungi of Temperate Europe, pp. 953, 959. o GBIF Species Record: https://www.gbif.org/species/5955029 o Lawrey et al, Mycological Research, 2009: https://www.academia.edu/download/84323014/j.mycres.2009.07.01620220417-1-1gscrbf.pdf o Larsson, Mycological Research 2007: https://www.crustfungi.com/pdf/larsson_2007.pdf o Larsson, Mycologia 2006: https://www.davidmoore.org.uk/21st_Century_Guidebook_to_Fungi_PLATINUM/REPRINT_collection/Larsson_etal_hymenochaetales.pdf o Ryvarden, Stereoid fungi of North America Synopsis Fungorum, 28 https://www.fungiflora.no/synopsis-47-stereoidfungi-a-synopsis o Crusts & Jells Species Record: https://www.aphyllo.net/spec.php?id=294600 (including Elia Martini’s own Crusts & Jells Excerpt with description and drawings: https://www.aphyllo.net/excerpts/ecj68_Muscinupta-laevis.pdf) • Useful Obs: The iNat Muscinupta obs in the U.S. with DNA do have a very “stipitate stereoid” appearance. description:
In bog

Lichen species provide **housing/shelter**, **symbiotic** within the lichen, & **construction**, wildlife & human

• **housing/shelter lichens**: lichens, a symbiotic partnership between fungi and algae/cyanobacteria; the algae/cyanobacteria provide food, the fungus **structural shelter** for algae/cyanobacteria, *etc*., also provide crucial **ecological shelter**, acting as habitats for invertebrates, and nesting materials for birds:

**Symbiosis** – **structural shelter**
◦ a basidiomycete fungus (a core partner yeast in the primary fungal partner's outer cortex, the 'skin') inaturalist.org/observations/301610979
◦ microbiome bacteria: (Proteobacteria), providing vitamins, growth hormones, & pathogen resistance  inaturalist.org/observations/301610979
◦ protists, kingdom Protista, on/in a lichen's microbiome (its entire community of microorganisms) inaturalist.org/observations/301610979
◦ bacteriophages (viruses infecting bacteria in bacterial communities within lichens; viruses also live in cytoplasm of hyphae in the lichen fungal partner (mycobiont) inaturalist.org/observations/301610979

**Construction** – **ecological shelter**
◦ invertebrate shelter: caterpillars, *e*.*g*., Psychidae family (Bagworm Moths), create protective, camouflaged bags using silk and specific lichens for shelter inaturalist.org/observations/226339273; Lichen-carrying Green Lacewing (*Leucochrysa pavida*) larvae inaturalist.org/observations/197251655
◦ wildlife habitat: lichens provide, or are found on, surfaces (like snags/dead wood) that offer food for small animals, birds, and insects; & shelter/nesting material inaturalist.org/observations/303710295
◦ artistic/functional usage: projects explore using lichens as artificial ("trans-species") wildlife housing

**– ...and also, "Coming Soon", even to a planet near you... -**

◦ artistic/functional usage: projects for people, like completely autonomous self-growing technology for expeditions to Mars developed by designing a synthetic community from multiple lichen species [stories.tamu.edu/news/2025/06/24/growing-homes-on-mars-texas-am-research-pioneers-autonomous-construction-using-synthetic-lichens/]

description: On *Eupatorium serotinum*

HRL3297

Date de récolte : 14 septembre 2020
Localité : Chibougamau

DESCRIPTION

Pileus de 4-12,5 mm de largeur, plano-convexe, déprimé au centre, devenant étalé et déprimé, hygrophane, strié par transparence, brun grisâtre (7D3, 7E3, 6F4) à l’état imbu, gris orangé à orange grisâtre (5B2, 5B3) au sec, glabre.

Lames décurrentes, espacées, concolores au chapeau, environ 1,5 mm de largeur

Stipe 12-26 x 0,75-1,5 mm, égal, luisant, glabre, brun foncé (7F4), parfois torsadé.

Odeur et saveur fortement farino-cucumiques.

Contexte concolore, très mince. 

Spores 5-7(8) x 3-3,5 µm, moy. 5,9 x 3,1 µm, Q = 1,67-2,33, Q moyen = 1,91 µm, oblongues à cylindriques

Basides: 22-26 x 5,5-6 µm, tétrasporiques, bouclées. 

Hyphes de la trame lamellaire bouclées.

Les spores sont un peu plus étroites que dans la description d'Arnolds, ce qui donne un Q un peu plus élevé. Outre cette différence, il n'existe aucune différence marquée avec l'espèce européenne. La forte odeur farino-cucumique est distinctive. Aucune séquence d'Omphalina microsperma n'est disponible dans les bases de données.
